Answer: C
Reason: Figure 1b demonstrates a massive right-sided pneumothorax with significant mediastinal shift to the left and an abnormal, distorted cardiac silhouette projecting into the right hemithorax, which is characteristic of right-sided cardiac herniation through a pericardial defect following pleurectomy/decortication for mesothelioma. This mechanical displacement explains the acute haemodynamic compromise (obstruction of venous return and cardiac output) better than simple tamponade or tension pneumothorax alone.
